answer.summary:
lamontae owns How the World Changes, with the existing playtester executing browser cases. Report six measured groups, each carrying actual source, setup and seed, initial and final game dates, unit, geography, coverage and intervention: material output and price levels AND rates, with the unemployment denominator and modelled housing; party vote and seat shares with contests, incumbency, coverage and outside-top-two share, keeping unlike offices apart; fixed-boundary regional change, with opinion and approval separate from votes and seats and with actual information and causal propagation; distinct ordinary-life contact and goal chains including open, lapsed, blocked and completed outcomes rather than inflated event counts; usable institutional authority, roles, action and delivery rather than raw person counts; and crisis origin, exposure, response, harm and recovery rather than a count of headlines. On method: use same-state and common-innovation intervention controls first, then explicit different seeds, and vary the actual setup.seed rather than only the questionnaire answers.

Extended 2026-09-22 15:58Z, answer C24 of ChatGPT's stress-test batch: divergence-metrics-and-what-to-test / what-should-we-be-testing: keep the already-acknowledged six groups; add eligible→considered→initiated→communicated→reachable→committed→applied→observed counts. Distinguish absent opportunity, unknown data, invalid authority, broken producer and invisible result. Match cohorts, exposure, time, geography and real setup.seed; use controlled positive fixtures separately from ordinary play. Do not force all rare event counts positive.

answer.stillOpen:
Two warnings worth keeping in front of whoever builds this. Equal exact arithmetic and legal constants are correct, so a constant-looking result is a lead rather than a failure to be cured by adding randomness. And surface fill is not a target: correctly empty differs from a missing producer, from unreachable, from stale and from broken, and scandals, news or debt must not be generated to fill a panel. ChatGPT also states that the 2-to-4 uniform opponent-count proposal in PR #393 is NOT approved by this answer.

Gates on the C24 extension, its words: "Do not force all rare event counts positive."

notes: Ownership, corrected after filing: the divergence lane ('How the world changes') owns the measurement and the report, and the playtesting lane has the browser instruments and town coverage and has offered to execute. This lane defines and hands over; it does not own either. An earlier note in this record said the shortlist should go to the playtesting lane, which named the wrong owner.

Metric 1 is the one this lane most wants, because it turns its own audit into something measurable: a value that is identical across seeds is a candidate constant, and that reverses the current order where a constant is found by reading and only then confirmed by play.

Two of lamontae's three examples are about drift compounding upward, from a place or a person to a region. Nothing measured so far speaks to that at all, so an honest answer may be that the game cannot yet produce the phenomenon he is asking to measure. If so, that is the answer worth having early rather than after a measurement programme is built.
One of six records from this sweep.

METHOD WARNING, measured here at 1c4992e8 and load-bearing for metric 1. worldSeedFor in src/presentation/new-game-identity.ts is a canonical encoding of the setup plus a digest, not a digest alone, and canonicalSetupEncoding carries exactly: seed, placeKey, startAge, optional birthMonth/birthDay, depth, startingLife, household, givenName, familyName, gender and pronouns only when stated, and startKind only on the custom route. The questionnaire is DELIBERATELY ABSENT — the file says so, because the seed is read mid-interview to choose the next question and a seed that moved with the answers would reshuffle the interview under the player. So a sameness test that varies only calibration answers will correctly produce one identical world and will read as a collapsed seed. That is a test defect wearing a game defect's clothes. Vary setup.seed, which is in the encoding, and pin which fields you varied in any null result.

The playtesting lane also offers contestFieldOpponentCount (draft PR #393) as a clean probe for metric 1: the first campaign value drawn from world.seed per contest, uniform over 2-4 at 4000 contests. Two seeds should disagree on it; agreement across every contest means something upstream is collapsing the seed. Not verified by this lane.
question: Two questions back to ChatGPT. First: of the metric points proposed below, which are worth reporting every time, which are missing, and which would mislead? Second, and this is lamontae's own ask: is there anything you would like us to test, in metrics or in play, that we are not testing?

sourcesChecked.source: The single-opponent defect, found by the playtest lane by walking fifteen towns
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It establishes why measures are needed rather than what they should be. Every race in America had exactly one opponent, from a literal count: 1 at nationwide-candidacy.ts:140 and campaign-projection.ts:670. Nothing about it looks wrong from inside one save; it is only visible as a sameness across saves. A divergence measure would have caught it in one run instead of fifteen towns.

sourcesChecked.source: The macro economy, measured by the 'What passing a law actually does' lane
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It proves divergence is already measurable and already happening: two lives run forward two years gave unemployment 3.57% to 3.85% on one seed and 4.23% to 4.82% on another, with inflation and a housing ratio alongside. It does not say which of those, at what granularity, belongs in a report, or what size of gap is signal.

sourcesChecked.source: The proposed metric points, offered for correction rather than as a decision
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: These are this lane's proposal and nothing more; no source establishes that they are the right ones. (1) Sameness across seeds: for a fixed route, how many of N saves produce the identical value — opponent count is the worked example, and any measure where N saves agree exactly is a suspected constant. (2) Party system shape: number of organizations winning any seat nationally, and the share held outside the two largest, which is lamontae's third-party question stated as a number. (3) Regional partisan drift: for a named region, the share of its seats held by each party at year 0 and year N, which is his popular-president example stated as a number. (4) Seated-world depth: people in the world, bodies with any member, and jurisdictions with a legislature, against the known floor that only the US Congress is seated. (5) Surface fill: for each player-reachable surface, whether it is non-empty on an ordinary first day, which is the pattern he wants reported. (6) Crisis incidence: how many crises occur in N years and how many a player could act on, which is his open question about the crisis system stated so it can be answered.

title: What to measure to show two saves diverging, and what ChatGPT wants tested
usableAnswer: A shortlist: the measures worth carrying in every report, each with what counts as a meaningful difference rather than noise, and anything proposed below that would mislead and why. Plus whatever ChatGPT wants tested, as concretely as it can put it — a named quantity, or a route through the game and what to look at when you get there.
whyItMatters: lamontae asked on 2026-09-22 for divergence to be tracked and for metric points to start appearing in these reports, and he named what he is most interested in: regional or local drift that ends up affecting the larger region. His examples were a very popular president turning the South reliably Democratic, the country developing a true third-party system, and how the crisis system behaves. Without agreed measures, every report says two saves 'felt different', which is exactly the claim-travels-further-than-its-measurement failure this project keeps paying for. He also asked directly that ChatGPT be given the chance to name what it wants tested rather than only answering what we bring.
